About SUDHIR TUTORIALS

1. History and Profile

SUDHIR TUTORIALS is a premier educational coaching institute founded with the singular vision of democratizing quality science, mathematics, and test-preparation education for high school and college students. Over the years, the institute has grown from a local physical tuition center into a digitally-empowered hub of academic excellence, catering to Class 6-12 curriculums and competitive exams like JEE Main/Advanced and NEET.

Recognizing the shift toward hybrid learning paradigms, SUDHIR TUTORIALS launched its integrated application platform in 2026 to bring premium administrative efficiency and academic support directly to the fingertips of parents, students, and educators.

By blending traditional pedagogical rigor with modern technological innovations, SUDHIR TUTORIALS has consistently achieved benchmark success, helping students secure top ranks in state board exams and national entrance tests. The platform acts as the core administrative and academic backbone of this mission.

2. Corporate Vision

To cultivate academic curiosity, analytical rigor, and critical thinking in every learner, transforming their potential into benchmark excellence through personalized, structured, and tech-driven educational pathways.

3. Mission Statements

  • Pedagogical Excellence: Delivering structured study resources, custom mock tests, and systematic progress trackings mapped to current national boards and syllabus patterns.
  • Digital Empowerment: Offering active support channels, such as the ST Guru ji AI Doubt Solver, to ensure students never experience blocks in their learning schedules.
  • Administrative Transparency: Providing clear online billing statements, automated fee invoices, and attendance logs to build transparency between the institute and families.
  • Community Connectivity: Fostering a secure environment for communications between students, parents, teachers, and administrators.

4. Strategic Goals

  1. Establish frictionless communication loops by transitioning DMs and group chats to our internal secure channel.
  2. Empower self-study and student independence by providing 24/7 academic query resolution using Gemini AI.
  3. Adopt a zero-paper administration process with the Billing Engine, automated receipts, and online test score publishing.
  4. Ensure scalable operation where any new teacher or admin can join the institute and immediately start working on the digital infrastructure using this handbook.

Chapter 1: Introduction & System Overview

The digital transformation of educational systems requires bridging administrative operations and academic support. SUDHIR TUTORIALS has built this custom web and native mobile application to consolidate all core learning, billing, and communication pathways into a secure, single-codebase environment.

1.1 Project Scope

This application replaces traditional classroom administration helpers, such as hard-copy attendance sheets, manual invoice books, PDF updates on general-purpose chat channels, and disparate messaging groups. By integrating these systems with Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, the application offers students round-the-clock help with homework doubts, provides teachers with automated slides generation tools, and offers administrators a powerful automated billing system.

1.2 Key System Modules

  • Role-Aware Dashboards: Custom portals for Students, Teachers, and Administrators, dynamically routed on session detection.
  • ST Guru ji AI Engine: A domain-locked multi-modal doubt solver accepting text, speech transcripts, images, and textbook PDF uploads.
  • Integrated Billing: Dynamic billing engine with scholarship logic, automatic late fine calculators, ledger lists, and print-ready receipts.
  • Real-time Messaging: Direct DMs and batch messaging channels updated via Server-Sent Events (SSE) instead of socket setups.
  • Mobile App Wrapper: Capacitor integration wrapping the live production URL, allowing instant updates and mobile-native FCM push notifications.
DEVELOPER ASSIGNMENT NOTICE: This guide contains the structural specs of the SUDHIR TUTORIALS system. Before initiating code revisions, verify that you have configured the environment keys (DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY) and synchronized the Prisma schema.

Chapter 2: Technology Stack & Core Rationale

Each layer of the SUDHIR TUTORIALS architecture is selected to minimize build overhead, maximize type safety, and maintain high responsiveness under serverless hosting environments.

2.1 Technical Stack Specifications

Stack Layer Technology Selected Purpose Rationale
Framework Next.js 15.5.18 Server routing, public pages, serverless API endpoints App router simplifies layout structuring, provides fast serverless cold starts, and ensures excellent SEO performance.
UI & Logic React 19 & TypeScript 5 Interactive client components & type interfaces TypeScript eliminates runtime data parsing exceptions across database schemas and endpoint returns.
ORM Prisma ORM 5.22.0 Database query construction and migrations Auto-generated type safety aligned with the Postgres tables, eliminating SQL syntax errors.
Database PostgreSQL (Supabase) Persistent storage with connection pool management Relational structure matches invoice relationships, user profiles, batch schedules, and message logs.
Authentication NextAuth.js v4 Session controls & HTTP-Only cookies Eliminates manual token refreshes and protects logins from Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
Mobile SDK Capacitor v8 Android native build wrapper Points natively to the live Vercel URL, allowing web updates to reflect instantly on mobile devices.
AI Model Google Gemini 2.5 Flash ST Guru ji LLM backend High token processing speed, rich multi-modal capability, and structured JSON output options.

2.2 Styling Strategy: Vanilla CSS

Instead of relying on Tailwind CSS or external component libraries, SUDHIR TUTORIALS uses Vanilla CSS variables declared in globals.css. This approach guarantees zero compile-time CSS translation delays, reduces resource size, and gives developers complete control over styles like glassmorphism and smooth animations. The theme variables switch dynamically on the :root element when light/dark mode is toggled, persisting selections via local storage.

Chapter 3: System Design & Architectural Patterns

The system is built on a Serverless Monolith model. Next.js handles server-side routing and database transactions, while delegating heavy computations (like LLM processing, audio transcription, and PDF parsing) to external specialized APIs.

3.1 Global Infrastructure Topology

Web Client
(React SPAs)
Mobile Client
(Android Native Wrapper)
▼ (HTTPS Request / SSE Feed)
Next.js Application Monolith (Hosted on Vercel)
Edge Middleware.ts REST APIs SSE EventHub NextAuth Manager
↙
↓
↘
PostgreSQL (Supabase)
Prisma Singleton / PgBouncer Connection Pool
Google Gemini LLM
gemini-2.5-flash API Streaming
FCM Push & CDNs
Capacitor Push Service & YouTube Embeds

Clients (Web browsers or the Capacitor Android WebView wrapper) access the system via HTTP for standard API transactions and establish a persistent Server-Sent Events (SSE) text stream for real-time messaging updates. The backend routes incoming requests to a single Next.js monolith instance, which accesses the central PostgreSQL database on Supabase using Prisma ORM. Deep-learning, AI reasoning, and voice transcriptions are executed on Google's Gemini API networks, isolating heavy loads from the web servers.

3.2 Architectural Sub-Services

  • Application Layer (Next.js): Hosts server-rendered public routes for marketing and coordinates dashboard portals. It handles REST endpoints using Next.js Serverless API routes.
  • Database Layer (PostgreSQL & Supabase): Restricts access using schema definitions. It uses PgBouncer to manage database connection pools and avoid database crashes during high-concurrency event loops.
  • AI Integration Gateway: Communicates with Google's API endpoints using custom backend routers. It enforces system prompts, parses PDF text extracts using pdf-parse, and formats streaming token responses into standard Server-Sent Event (SSE) chunks.
  • Push Notification Broker: Integrates Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to push native notifications to registered Android mobile device tokens when background events (like fee billing or urgent alerts) occur.

3.3 Database Connection Pool & Retry Lifecycle

1. Serverless Execution Hook Initiated
▼
2. Reference Global Prisma Client (Singleton Check)
↙ (Existing)
Reuse Database Connection
↘ (None)
Instantiate New Prisma Client
▼
3. Transaction Encapsulated in withDbRetry Block
▼
4. Execution Success?
↙ (Yes)
Return Query Results
↘ (No - Transient Error)
Trigger Exponential Backoff (1s -> 2s -> 4s)
▼
Retry Database Connection (Max 3)

In a serverless environment, database connection pools can be exhausted quickly due to brief server instantiations. SUDHIR TUTORIALS solves this by using a global singleton pattern for the Prisma Client. Furthermore, all query logic is wrapped in a retry handler (withDbRetry) that catches transient database connection errors and automatically retries execution up to three times with exponential backoff (1000ms -> 2000ms -> 4000ms), maintaining high reliability during brief database drops.

3.4 User Onboarding Gate Pipeline

1. Enter Credentials (/login)
▼
2. Bcrypt Validation in NextAuth Handler
▼
3. Issue Secure HTTP-Only JWT Cookie
▼
4. Check onboardingCompleted & mustChangePassword
↙ (False)
Redirect to /onboarding
↘ (True)
Check isProfileVerified
↙ (False)
Lock at /waiting-verification
↘ (True)
Route to /dashboard/student

This multi-stage security gate prevents unauthorized account activity. Newly provisioned accounts are forced to the onboarding page to configure passwords and Recovery PINs. Their profiles are then locked in a pending verification queue until an administrator reviews and approves them, unlocking full platform access.

Chapter 5: Authentication, Security & Cryptography

SUDHIR TUTORIALS uses a strict, role-based security model to protect authentication credentials, prevent session hijacking, and safeguard personal student data.

5.1 Password Hashing Lifecycle

All passwords are encrypted on the server side using the bcryptjs library. The system uses 12 salt rounds, protecting against brute-force and dictionary attacks. The database never stores passwords in plain text.

5.2 Credentials Validation Flow

NextAuth.js handles the login process using a credentials provider model. The authentication flow follows these steps:

// NextAuth Authorize API Logic Snippet
async authorize(credentials) {
  if (!credentials?.username || !credentials?.password) {
    throw new Error("Missing username or password fields.");
  }
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
    where: { username: credentials.username }
  });
  if (!user || !user.isActive) {
    throw new Error("User account not found or deactivated.");
  }
  const isValid = await bcrypt.compare(credentials.password, user.passwordHash);
  if (!isValid) {
    throw new Error("Invalid login credentials.");
  }
  return {
    id: user.id,
    name: user.name,
    role: user.role,
    mustChangePassword: user.mustChangePassword,
    onboardingCompleted: user.onboardingCompleted,
    isProfileVerified: user.isProfileVerified
  };
}

5.3 Recovery PIN & One-Time Passwords

To assist users who forget their passwords without exposing database vulnerabilities, the system features a 4-digit Recovery PIN. During onboarding, users configure a Recovery PIN, which is encrypted using bcrypt. If a password reset is requested, users provide their username and 4-digit PIN. The system validates the PIN and permits password resets without administrative intervention.

For younger students, administrators can generate temporary One-Time Passwords (OTPs) through the dashboard user profile modal, bypassing the standard email-based reset flow.

Chapter 6: Role-Based Authorization & Session Control

System access is strictly segmented by user roles: STUDENT, TEACHER, and ADMIN. Edge middleware intercepts and checks incoming requests before executing database transactions.

6.1 Role Access Matrix

Functional Operation Student Teacher Admin
View Personal Fee Ledger Read-Only No Access Full Access
Mark Batch Attendance No Access Write / Update Full Access
Create Courses & Batches No Access No Access Full Access
Assign Fee Invoices No Access No Access Full Access
ST Guru ji Mode Doubt Solver (Student) Lesson Planner (Teacher) Lesson Planner (Admin)
Delete Chat Messages Self Only Self Only Global Clean

6.2 Middleware Edge Gates (middleware.ts)

Next.js Edge Middleware checks incoming request headers. If a user tries to access a path that doesn't match their role (e.g., a student trying to access /dashboard/admin), the middleware blocks the request and redirects them to the login page.

// Dynamic Middleware Check
const token = await getToken({ req });
const path = req.nextUrl.pathname;

if (!token) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/login", req.url));
}
if (path.startsWith("/dashboard/admin") && token.role !== "ADMIN") {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/unauthorized", req.url));
}

Additionally, if the user has mustChangePassword === true, the middleware forces them to the /onboarding page, preventing them from accessing any dashboard tabs until their password is updated.

The StudentLedger.tsx component provides a detailed view of the student's billing statements, listing all generated invoices, applied discounts, late fines, payments, and outstanding balances. It includes a print-ready mode, allowing parents to print records directly from their browsers.

Chapter 8: Teacher Portal & Classroom Automation

The teacher dashboard provides tools for marking attendance, scheduling mock tests, uploading study resources, and generating lesson plans.

8.1 Attendance Management

The attendance tab lists all batches assigned to the teacher. Selecting a batch loads a roster of enrolled students. The teacher can mark each student as PRESENT, ABSENT, or LATE. The system validates the entries and updates the database, recalculating the student's attendance percentage.

8.2 Lesson Planning & Slide Generation (Prepare Mode)

To help teachers prepare for classes, ST Guru ji includes a "Prepare Mode". By entering a topic, class level, and slide count, the system queries the Gemini API to generate structured presentation slides. The response is returned in a clean JSON format, containing slides like:

  • TITLE: Main topic slide.
  • CONCEPT: Core academic definition slides.
  • FORMULA: Mathematical equation slides.
  • DERIVATION: Step-by-step proofs.
  • EXAM_PREP: Typical exam questions.
  • MCQ: Multiple-choice questions for class interaction.

Teachers can review slides, edit the content inline, switch between slide and lesson notes views, and download the slides for classroom use.

Chapter 9: Admin Panel & Institutional Controls

The Admin Panel is the administrative control center of SUDHIR TUTORIALS, managing users, billing cycles, batch schedules, and student admissions.

9.1 User Directory & Profile Management

The Users tab features a searchable user directory. Clicking a user card opens the UserProfileModal, allowing administrators to edit profile fields, assign base fees, reset passwords, or deactivate accounts.

New admissions and job applications are processed through dedicated review queues, allowing administrators to approve applications and instantly create corresponding user profiles.

9.2 The Auto-Billing Engine

The billing engine automates the monthly fee generation process. It uses a single action to process active students and generate invoices based on their profiles:

// Conceptual Billing Engine Logic
const students = await prisma.user.findMany({
  where: { role: "STUDENT", isActive: true, isProfileVerified: true },
  include: { studentProfile: true }
});

const invoices = students.map(student => {
  const base = student.studentProfile?.baseFee || 0;
  const scholarshipPct = student.studentProfile?.scholarship || 0;
  const discount = base * (scholarshipPct / 100);
  
  return prisma.payment.create({
    data: {
      studentId: student.id,
      title: "Monthly Fee",
      billingMonth: "2026-06",
      dueDate: new Date("2026-06-20"),
      amount: base,
      discount: discount,
      status: "PENDING"
    }
  });
});
await Promise.all(invoices);

Administrators run the billing engine at the start of each month, automatically applying scholarship discounts and generating payment records.

Chapter 11: ST Guru ji – AI Doubt Solver System

ST Guru ji is the AI tutoring core of the platform, built on Google Gemini to deliver fast, academic responses.

11.1 Multimodal Input Processing Flow

1. User Inputs Question (Text, Voice, Image, or PDF)
▼
2. API Route (/api/student/guru-ji) Validates Session
▼
3. Multi-modal Extraction (pdf-parse / Base64 images / audio)
▼
4. Prompt Guardrail: Academic Validator
↙ (Non-Academic)
Refuse query & show Decorum Warning
↘ (Academic)
Call Gemini 2.5 Flash API Stream
▼
5. Stream SSE Chunks to Client UI (Typewriter effect)
▼
6. Save Interaction to DoubtHistory Table

11.2 Multi-modal Inputs

  • Text Input: Standard typed questions.
  • Image Input: Photos of equations or textbook questions, processed directly by Gemini's vision capability.
  • PDF Uploads: Uses the pdf-parse library to extract text from documents, passing the content to the AI engine.
  • Voice Input: Audio recordings are transcribed into text on the server side, allowing students to speak their questions.

11.3 Fallback System

If the Gemini API is unavailable or times out, the system uses a local, rule-based fallback engine (generateAcademicResponse). This fallback uses regex pattern matching to detect common academic topics (e.g., photosynthesis, quadratic equations, Newton's laws) and returns pre-configured explanations in English or Hindi.

11.4 Decorum Warnings & Language Handling

The system prompt enforces strict rules. The AI will refuse non-academic queries (e.g., entertainment, games) and warn the user: "Please maintain decorum and focus on your studies. Any inappropriate queries will be reported to the administration."

The system automatically detects English, Hindi, and Hinglish, responding in the same language. The frontend parses the streaming markdown, rendering headers as styled bold text and removing raw # symbols for a cleaner reading experience.

Chapter 12: Integrated Billing & Fee Management

The platform features a comprehensive billing and fee tracking system, automating invoicing, late fine calculations, and payment verification.

12.1 Auto-Billing Workflow

1. Admin configures baseFee & scholarship in Student Profile
▼
2. Billing Engine executes Monthly Invoice Cycle
▼
3. Discount = baseFee * scholarship% (Invoice Net Created)
▼
4. Overdue Limit Reached? -> Apply Late Fine (days * fineRate)
▼
5. Student Pays (CASH / UPI Proof)
▼
6. Admin verifies payment -> Status marked as VERIFIED

12.2 Late Fine Calculations

If an invoice is unpaid past its due date, the billing engine automatically applies a late fine. The fine is calculated dynamically: currentLateFine = daysOverdue * dailyFineRate. The daily fine rate is configured in the global system settings. The fine updates automatically when the student views the invoice or when the admin reviews the dashboard.

12.3 Credit Balances

If a student pays more than their outstanding balance, the excess amount is saved as a credit balance. The credit balance is automatically applied to offset the next generated invoice, reducing the total due.

12.4 Fee Verification

When a student submits an offline cash payment or uploads a transaction ID for a UPI transfer, the invoice status changes to PENDING_VERIFICATION. The admin reviews the transaction details and marks the payment as VERIFIED, updating the fee records and locking the invoice.

Chapter 13: SSE Messaging & Real-Time Engine

To support real-time messaging without the overhead of WebSockets, SUDHIR TUTORIALS utilizes Server-Sent Events (SSE) for instant message delivery.

13.1 SSE Communication Architecture

1. User A sends message via POST /api/messages
▼
2. Server saves message to database via Prisma Client
▼
3. Server fires message event on Global EventEmitter
▼
4. User B's active connection /api/messages/subscribe intercepts event
▼
5. Message pushed down SSE text/event-stream -> UI updates

13.2 Connection Lifecycle

When a user opens the chat tab, the browser establishes a persistent HTTP connection to /api/messages/subscribe. The server keeps the connection open, sending heartbeat events to prevent timeouts. The subscription uses simple headers:

Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive

13.3 Real-time Features

  • Read Receipts: When a user opens a chat thread, the system triggers a request to mark messages as read, updating the sender's screen with double tick indicators.
  • File & Image Sharing: Users can upload attachments within chat threads. Files are uploaded via the server, and the resulting URL is sent as a message payload.
  • Message Editing & Deletion: Users can edit their messages within a 4-minute window. Deletions can be performed for the sender only or for both parties, updating the UI in real time.

Chapter 14: Mobile App Architecture & Capacitor Layer

The native Android app uses Capacitor, running the live production Next.js website inside a secure, native WebView. This setup ensures that web updates reflect instantly on mobile devices without requiring manual app updates.

14.1 Native Device Integration

  • Push Notifications: On login, the app registers with Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). The resulting push token is saved to the user's database profile via POST /api/user/push-token. When notifications are triggered, a backend service sends FCM payloads, displaying alerts on the student's device.
  • App Update Checker: The AppUpdateChecker component periodically queries /api/app-version. If the server version is newer than the installed version, the app displays a prompt directing the user to the Play Store to update.
  • Back Button Manager: The CapacitorBackButtonManager intercepts native back button presses. It closes open modals or navigates to the previous dashboard tab, preventing the app from exiting unexpectedly.

This hybrid approach combines the development speed of web frameworks with the integration features of native mobile applications.

Chapter 15: API Reference & Endpoint Definitions (Part 1)

All core functionalities are exposed via RESTful API routes. These routes enforce authentication and require matching user roles.

15.1 Authentication APIs

  • POST /api/auth/[...nextauth]: NextAuth endpoint for session creation.
  • POST /api/auth/forgot-password: Resets user passwords using valid Recovery PIN hashes.

15.2 Student APIs

  • GET /api/student/dashboard: Returns dashboard statistics, including upcoming tests, attendance percentages, and pending bills.
  • GET /api/student/fees: Lists all invoices generated for the student.
  • POST /api/student/fees/pay: Initiates payment flows and records transaction reference details.
  • GET /api/student/fees/receipt/[id]: Generates a downloadable PDF receipt for a paid invoice.
  • POST /api/student/guru-ji: Process ST Guru ji queries, streaming answers via Server-Sent Events.
  • GET /api/student/guru-ji/history: Returns the student's past doubts history log.
  • DELETE /api/student/guru-ji/history?id=[id]: Deletes a doubt history item.
  • POST /api/student/guru-ji/transcribe: Transcribes voice messages into text.

15.3 Teacher APIs

  • GET /api/teacher/classes: Returns batches assigned to the teacher.
  • POST /api/teacher/attendance: Submits attendance records for a batch.
  • POST /api/teacher/materials: Uploads study materials.
  • POST /api/teacher/tests: Creates new mock tests.
  • POST /api/teacher/test-results: Submits student test scores.

Chapter 15: API Reference & Endpoint Definitions (Part 2)

Administrative and real-time messaging APIs support user management, billing operations, and group communications.

15.4 Admin Control APIs

  • GET /api/admin/overview: Returns global administrative statistics (revenue, student counts, verifications).
  • POST /api/admin/users: Provisions new student or teacher accounts.
  • GET /api/admin/verify: Returns users awaiting profile verification.
  • POST /api/admin/finances/auto-assign: Triggers the billing engine for a specific month.
  • POST /api/admin/salaries: Creates teacher salary records.
  • POST /api/admin/students/promote: Bulk promotes students to the next class level.
  • GET /api/admin/admissions: Lists submitted public admission inquiries.

15.5 Messaging APIs

  • GET /api/messages: Fetches conversation logs between two users.
  • POST /api/messages: Sends a message.
  • POST /api/messages/read: Marks messages in a chat thread as read.
  • GET /api/messages/subscribe: SSE subscription route for real-time messaging updates.
  • POST /api/messages/upload: Handles uploading of images and files within a message thread.

Chapter 16: UI Component Library Documentation

All user interfaces are built using modular React components, designed to adapt cleanly to both mobile and desktop screen sizes.

16.1 Key Interface Components

  • ChatWindow.tsx: Manages chat channels, contacts directories, unread counts, and file uploads. It updates in real time using SSE subscriptions.
  • Sidebar.tsx: A role-aware navigation bar. It collapses on mobile layouts and displays badges for unread notifications and messages.
  • StudentLedger.tsx: Details invoices, applied discounts, late fines, and payments, formatted for clean printing.
  • ProfileEditor.tsx: Allows users to update their profile information and upload photos.
  • ScholarshipPredictor3D.tsx: Calculates eligible scholarships based on academic scores, featuring a 3D flipping card layout.
  • BugReportModal.tsx: Lets users submit issues directly to administrators for review.

16.2 Design Consistency

Layout components use glassmorphism styles and CSS transitions. Inputs, buttons, cards, and modal components share colors and styles, maintaining design consistency across the application.

Chapter 17: Enterprise Security & Compliance

The application implements multiple security layers to protect database queries, validate API requests, and handle transient errors.

17.1 Security Best Practices

  • SQL Injection Prevention: Prisma ORM parameterizes all database queries by default, blocking SQL injection attempts.
  • Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation: Session tokens are stored in secure, HTTP-only cookies, preventing access via client-side JavaScript.
  • Input Validation: Form submissions and API payloads are validated using Zod schemas, rejecting unexpected data.
  • Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Protection: NextAuth.js uses CSRF tokens to validate state-changing requests, blocking unauthorized actions.

17.2 Database Retry Wrapper (withDbRetry)

To prevent connection failures in serverless environments, database transactions are wrapped in a retry function (withDbRetry). This wrapper automatically retries failed database operations up to three times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), helping maintain session stability during transient database connection drops.

Chapter 18: Infrastructure Setup & Deployment Runbook

Follow these steps to deploy and configure the SUDHIR TUTORIALS application platform.

18.1 Setup Commands

# 1. Clone the repository and install project dependencies
git clone https://github.com/SudhirSir/SudhirTutorials.git
cd SudhirTutorials
npm install

# 2. Configure environment keys
# Create a .env file and configure:
# DATABASE_URL="postgresql://username:password@host:port/database"
# NEXTAUTH_SECRET="your-nextauth-secret-key"
# NEXTAUTH_URL="https://yourdomain.com"
# GEMINI_API_KEY="your-google-gemini-key"

# 3. Synchronize database schemas and run database seeds
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
node seed.mjs

# 4. Compile the production application bundle
npm run build

# 5. Build and synchronize native Android app
npx cap sync android
npx cap open android

18.2 Connection Pool Settings

In serverless deployments, database connections can build up quickly. Ensure database connections are managed as singletons on the server, and verify that connection pooling is configured on your Supabase database dashboard to prevent pool exhaustion.
